newsitem.title: UK: Reed sells division of Reed books.
newsitem.headline: Reed sells division of Reed books.

text.p: Anglo-Dutch publishing group Reed-Elsevier said on Friday it has agreed to sell the adult Trade division of Reed Books to publisher Random House.
It gave no financial details but said that it intends to sell the rest of Reed Books in due course, which comprises the divisions of Children's, Illustrated and Reference.

Reed said that the adult trade division includes the authors Roddy Doyle, Umberto Eco, Graham Greene, George Orwell and Sue Townsend. It includes well known trade names William Heinemann, Mandarin Paperbacks, Methuen, Minerva, Secker & Warburg and Sinclair Stevenson.

"The adult fiction market is polarising between very large companies able to take advantage of significant economies of scale and small specialist businesses serving niche sectors," said John Holloran, chief Executive of Reed Books.
"By joining with Random House the division will now be part of a group dedicated to being a major leader in UK trade publishing," he added.
Reed shares were trading 11-1/2 pence higher in London at 1060 pence by 1029 GMT.
